limitations: The benchmark measures cell-level tasks only: it excludes donor- and sample-level tasks, such as predicting a donor's disease state, which the report says Stack's use of the other cells of a sample helps.

Systems run under different conditions: Stack uses batch labels at inference, SCimilarity and scPRINT were trained with cell-type labels, and PCA is fitted to each atlas. Each evaluation's comparison.adaptation states its system's condition, so results from different conditions are not compared automatically.
No uncertainty is printed for any value under this protocol.

Raw integer counts of human genes with all measured genes; genes outside HyCell's 36,495-gene vocabulary are dropped, and measured zeros are drawn from the genes the dataset measures, so a preselected highly-variable-gene matrix is not a valid input.
Developer-run: the authors chose the atlases, the metrics, the composite weights and ran every comparator.
attributes.scope_note: Eleven pretrained models and PCA, every one rerun by the HyCell authors on the same cells and scored by one implementation built on scib-metrics on the absolute scale. attributes.extraction_method: pdftotext -layout text layer, parsed by extract/parse.py with every row label and cell count asserted.
limitations: Author-released report, not peer reviewed. The developer of HyCell ran every model, so no result is independent of the developer.
No uncertainty is printed anywhere in the report: no interval, standard deviation or test for any score, including the 0.735 against 0.736 comparison with Stack.

The comparators do not run under equal conditions. Stack encodes sets of 256 cells with the cells of each batch together, so it uses batch labels at inference; SCimilarity and scPRINT are trained with cell-type labels; PCA is fitted to each evaluation atlas on 2,000 highly variable genes. HyCell embeds each cell from its own counts with no batch or donor information.

The benchmark measures cell-level tasks only. Stack draws on the other cells of a sample at inference, which the report says helps sample-level tasks such as predicting a donor's disease state; such tasks are not in the benchmark.

The composite S = 0.3 Bio + 0.2 Batch + 0.25 LR + 0.25 kNN is the authors' chosen weighting. Table 4 prints only S per atlas, not its four components per atlas, so the per-atlas weighting cannot be checked.
